title: GloCTM: Cross-Lingual Topic Modeling via a Global Context Space
subcategory: dual-pathway cross-lingual NTM with a global context space
task: Cross-lingual topic modelling for bilingual corpora
problem: Existing cross-lingual models learn topics in disjoint language spaces and rely on dictionaries, giving loosely connected topic spaces and ignoring multilingual pretrained semantics.
architecture: Polyglot augmentation enriches each BoW with intra- and cross-lingual word neighbours found with multilingual embeddings, giving a global BoW over the joint vocabulary; a global encoder and language-specific local encoders infer topic proportions, kept consistent by a KL loss; a global topic-word matrix built from both language pathways synchronises topics; a Centered Kernel Alignment loss aligns topic proportions with multilingual PLM embeddings.
llm_or_encoder: Multilingual word embeddings and multilingual PLM embeddings; LLM ratings for evaluation
key_results: Rakuten Amazon: CNPMI 0.040 and TQ 0.037 vs 0.033 (InfoCTM) and 0.027 (XTRA).
Amazon Review: TQ 0.056 vs 0.050 for XTRA; EC News: TQ 0.070, tied with XTRA.
strengths: Builds cross-lingual alignment into the input, encoder and decoder rather than relying only on auxiliary losses.
Clear gains in cross-lingual (train in one language, test in another) classification.

limitations.text: Topic uniqueness is below XTRA on Amazon Review (0.958 vs 0.976) and Rakuten Amazon (0.925 vs 0.971).
On EC News, CNPMI (0.071) is below the clustering baselines u-SVD (0.082) and SVD-LR (0.083).
No limitations section; evaluated only on two language pairs.
